name: Puwagaan Kaan (Healing Home), opened as Tawi Kaan Apartments
headline: The Piñon Project and BlueLine Development built Puwagaan Kaan, renamed Tawi Kaan ('our home' in Ute), 42 permanent supportive apartments for families leaving homelessness at 560 E. Empire St. in Cortez, all at 30% AMI with Division of Housing vouchers and a Ute preference, using $1,233,450 a year in 2022 federal 9% credits; it opened on 2024-10-15.
why_it_matters: It is Montezuma County's first supportive housing and a working model of tribe-partnered PSH off reservation: the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe helped design it, supplies a tribal liaison, and its members get a preference, with a local housing authority as special limited partner for tax savings.

status.label: Built and open (opened 2024-10-15)
status.detail: The Journal reports Tawi Kaan opened on 2024-10-15, and CHFA's own partner story describes its completion. Linking Tawi Kaan to the CHFA ledger name Puwagaan Kaan is inferred: same sponsors, 42 units in a 14/14/14 mix, all at 30% AMI, on Empire Street, and CHFA cites its $1.2M 9% award. No 8609 record was found.

next_step: Confirm the 8609 year and final credit in CHFA or HUD placed-in-service data, and the Montezuma County Housing Authority special limited partnership terms.

facts.value: 560 E. Empire St., Cortez, CO 81321 (CHFA lists 'TBD Empire St.')
N, PSH: new construction, permanent supportive housing
About 3 acres, zoned R2, bought by The Piñon Project in October 2020; next to an Axis Health clinic site; vacant and level

Three stories, Type V wood frame, U-shaped around an enclosed courtyard with fire pit and play area; over 4,500 sq ft of amenity and service space; 84 parking spaces planned; furnished units; washer/dryer in three-bedroom units; NGBS certification
Conditional Use Permit approved unanimously by Cortez City Council on January 11 (2022, inferred from the application date) for the use and density
Ute Mountain Ute Tribe passed a resolution of support, a tribal council member sat on the design team, the tribe chose the name, and it provides a full-time tribal liaison

Boston Financial is named as an investor partner.
Homeless Solutions Program grant funds and Enhanced Development Gap funds planned; 42 project-based vouchers; Tenancy Support Services funding sought.
Planned at application; a waiver of the 1.30 maximum debt coverage ratio was requested.

background.text: Origin: Cortez was one of six rural communities chosen in 2020 for a Colorado Health Foundation supportive housing technical assistance pilot.
Market at application: zero vacancy and only six existing 30% AMI units in the market area; waitlists of 179 at the Montezuma housing authority and 207 families at the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe.
Outreach: four public meetings (two in January 2021, two in January 2022) plus tribal council video meetings.
Operating cash flow was projected to cover only 17% of the services budget; the rest relies on partners, DOH services money and CHFA's developer fee boost.
The application narrative also calls the project 'Piñon Apartments' and 'Healing Homes' in places.
